title: The smooth-proper cohomological family
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq0}$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. For every prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $K_{X,\ell}=(\Ql)_X$ be the constant Weil
sheaf, and let $F_\ell$ be the global geometric Frobenius on
$\RGamma(X,K_{X,\ell})$, using the geometric-Frobenius convention
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Fix an indeterminate $T$. For every integer $i$ with
$0\leq i\leq2d$, define

$$
 V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql),
\qquad
 F_{i,\ell}=F_\ell\vert_{V_{i,\ell}}.
$$

The finiteness of the spaces $V_{i,\ell}$, the invertibility of the operators
$F_{i,\ell}$, and the vanishing of $H^i(X,\Ql)$ outside $0\leq i\leq2d$ are
the cohomological-finiteness proposition, and are not part of the definition
of the family. Define

$$
 P_{i,\ell}(T)=
 \det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})\in\Ql[T].
$$

It has constant coefficient $1$, degree $\dim_{\Ql}V_{i,\ell}$, and leading
coefficient $(-1)^{\dim V_{i,\ell}}\det(F_{i,\ell})$.

mathlib_searches.results: Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Proetale.lean (big and small pro-étale site, after Bhatt–Scholze); Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/ElladicCohomology.lean: `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ellAdicSheaf` (the sheaf U ↦ C(U, ℤ_[ℓ]) on the pro-étale site) and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EllAdicCohomology` (the groups Hⁱ(X, ℤ_[ℓ])). Nothing on Weil sheaves, a Frobenius action, ℚ_ℓ-coefficients, finiteness, or det(1 - T F | Hⁱ)
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: Mathlib has the integral ℓ-adic cohomology groups of a scheme on the pro-étale site but not the family (V_{i,ℓ}, F_{i,ℓ}, P_{i,ℓ}); only the linear-algebra notions of the statement are leaves

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against its source (master blueprint, order 2856): verbatim, kept; slopmaster2 has no copy of this node. Named every notion the statement is built from. Kept the seven imported statement dependencies, each verified to supply what is used: the datum p,a,q,k_0,k, the geometric fiber X, the prime l and Q_l (def-weil-finite-field-fiber); smooth, proper, geometrically connected, pure dimension d (def-weil-geometric-hypotheses); the geometric-Frobenius convention g_X (def-weil-frobenius-detailed); Weil sheaves and D^b_{c,W}(X,E) with E=Q_l (def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex); RGamma, H^i and the constant coefficient object (Q_l)_X with its canonical Weil structure (def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology); F_l on RGamma and its action on H^i, i.e. F_{i,l} (def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius); prop-cohomological-finiteness, which the statement names and which the definition relies on for V_{i,l} to be finite-dimensional (so that det(1 - T F_{i,l} | V_{i,l}) is meaningful) and for F_{i,l} to be invertible (used by the degree claim). Added the linear-algebra notions, as new Mathlib leaves: polynomial ring Q_l[T] (def-weil-polynomial-ring, Polynomial), dimension (def-weil-vector-space-dimension, Module.finrank), determinant of an endomorphism (def-weil-endomorphism-determinant, LinearMap.det), the reverse characteristic polynomial det(1 - T F | V) (def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial, Matrix.charpolyRev), and the existing leaf def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace (FiniteDimensional). The last sentence of the statement is an assertion, not part of the definition: it is stated as the new node lem-weil-reverse-charpoly-coefficients (unsplit; Mathlib has its ingredients), which, together with prop-cohomological-finiteness for invertibility, is what the sentence rests on. Recorded a Mathlib search for the item itself: Mathlib has H^i(X, Z_l) on the pro-étale site (AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/ElladicCohomology.lean) but no Weil structure, Frobenius or Q_l-coefficients.
